correctness.rationale: For a primitive field seed \(a\) the two Fermat quotient constraints are independent affine equations in the first lift variable except when their unique forbidden roots coincide; the derivative of \(x+\varepsilon x^{-1}\) does not vanish for \(p\ge7\). Thus there are exactly \(p-2+\delta\) successful lifts to \(p^2\). Primitive roots modulo \(p^2\) remain primitive under all higher lifts, so the factor is exactly \(p^{k-2}\). Direct seed-existence exceptions checked at 3, 5, 7, 13, 61; seed existence at all remaining primes is Corollary 2 of arxiv:1711.06392. Code verified 44 prime-square cases, 24 prime-cube fibers, but finite cases do not prove the theorem.

originality.rationale: The motivating explicit prime-power primitive-root conjecture is Sun arxiv:1405.0290, Conjecture 4.10. Cohen et al. arxiv:1711.06392 Corollary 2 proves field-level seed existence, not the prime-power ring lift counts. Carella arxiv:2501.10399 considers a different averaged cross-level primitive root problem. Relevant research record results concern cyclotomic Hensel lifts, additive geometry of modular hyperbolas, or p-adic congruence towers, rather than simultaneous primitive Laurent values. Unindexed historical equivalents remain a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: A prior unindexed solution of Sun Conjecture 4.10 or an equivalent elementary two-obstruction lifting lemma could cover the existence statement or even the multiplicity formula.
The finite-field seed classification is imported from Corollary 2; this package does not reprove its nontrivial field-existence argument.
Some historically relevant texts were available only as abstracts or bibliographic records, so no absence claim is made about their full contents.

value.rationale: Solves Sun’s specific named prime-power existence conjecture by combining an independently established finite-field seed theorem with a uniform exact lift count. The new structural invariant is the coincidence/noncoincidence of the two forbidden p² lifts, yielding p−1 versus p−2 choices for each finite-field primitive seed and all exponents. This is a motivated complete local classification, not arbitrary finite enumeration; it does not claim a closed count of seeds or least primitive witnesses.
